advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the Windows claim in the c2ba docstring (and check the _exe_stub docstring) that git spawned via exec_real is in the launcher's kill-on-close job, or add a test proving that a grandchild dies when the stub is killed
evidence: tests/unit/test_store_write_git_timeout_c2ba.py:81: POSIX it ``exec``s git in the same process; on Windows git runs inside the stub launcher's
tests/unit/test_store_write_git_timeout_c2ba.py:83: kill. A watchdog kill therefore takes down whatever is doing the work,
tests/_exe_stub.py prelude: `sys.exit(subprocess.call(argv))` on non-POSIX, so the real tool is a grandchild of the launcher, not its direct child
tests/test_exe_stub.py test_a_timeout_kill_ends_the_stub_and_releases_its_pipes only exercises the `hang` branch (time.sleep in the body), not a kill after exec_real has spawned the real tool
Absence: no test checks that a grandchild spawned by exec_real dies when the stub is killed on Windows
advisory.finding: The c2ba fixture docstring says that on Windows the real git 'runs inside the stub launcher's kill-on-close job' and 'nothing is orphaned'. distlib's launcher (derived from the py launcher) assigns only its direct child (the Python body) to the job, and that job allows silent breakaway. So the git spawned by exec_real's subprocess.call would probably not be in the job and would survive a watchdog kill of the launcher. The claim is unverified: tests/test_exe_stub.py only tests a body that sleeps in-process, never one that has handed off to the real tool through exec_real.
scenarios: On Windows, if the watchdog fires after the 1.63 s sleep, while the real `git commit` is running, git keeps running and holding .git/index.lock and may still complete the commit that the test asserts was lost

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a tests/test_exe_stub.py case whose stub body calls `exec_real([sys.executable, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(60)"])`. Run it with `subprocess.run(..., capture_output=True, timeout=2)`, assert TimeoutExpired, and assert the call returns well under 60 s.
evidence:
tests/_exe_stub.py prelude (added): "def exec_real(argv):
    if os.name == "posix":
        os.execv(argv[0], argv)
    sys.stdout.flush()
    sys.exit(subprocess.call(argv))"

tests/_exe_stub.py docstring (added): "on Windows, where ``os.execv`` returns to the caller before the new program finishes, it runs ``argv`` as a child and exits with its status." and "The launcher puts its child in a kill-on-close job, so a watchdog that kills the stub also kills the Python process running the body." It says nothing about the grandchild that `exec_real` spawns.
tests/test_exe_stub.py fixture body (added): "if sys.argv[1:2] == [\"hang\"]:\n            time.sleep(60)". The hang branch returns before `exec_real` is reached.
tests/test_exe_stub.py test_a_timeout_kill_ends_the_stub_and_releases_its_pipes only runs `subprocess.run(["git", "hang"], capture_output=True, timeout=2, check=False)`.

tests/unit/test_store_write_git_timeout_c2ba.py docstring (added): "on Windows git runs inside the stub launcher's kill-on-close job. A watchdog kill therefore takes down whatever is doing the work, sleeping or committing". This claim covers the exec_real child and has no test behind it.
advisory.finding: tests/test_exe_stub.py does not test a watchdog kill that arrives while `exec_real` is running the real program. On Windows the prelude runs `argv` with `subprocess.call` as a grandchild of the launcher, so the helper's claim that nothing is orphaned and the pipes are released is unverified on exactly the path the c2ba fixture's docstring relies on. If that grandchild survives the kill, it keeps the captured pipes open and `subprocess.run(..., timeout=...)` blocks on it. The one timeout test uses a body that sleeps in the stub process itself (`time.sleep(60)`) and never calls `exec_real`, so it cannot catch this.
scenarios: Windows sweep: a watchdog fires while the real git (started by exec_real via subprocess.call) is still running. If the launcher's job lets that grandchild break away, git outlives the kill and holds stdout/stderr open, so subprocess.run waits for git and the watchdog tests hang or time out.
A future edit to the prelude, such as adding a creationflag or dropping the flush, breaks kill propagation to the exec_real child, and no test on any OS notices.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a fixture branch, e.g. `if sys.argv[1:2] == ["hang-child"]: exec_real([sys.executable, "-c", "import time; time.sleep(60)"])`. Add a test mirroring test_a_timeout_kill_ends_the_stub_and_releases_its_pipes for `["git", "hang-child"]`, so a kill during exec_real is verified on POSIX (the process replaced by os.execv) and on Windows (the grandchild started by subprocess.call).
